acceptance_items.description: The documented retrospective technical sample-size calculation uses the inverse-square-root method under a 5% significance level, 80% power, and a directional test.
acceptance_criteria: The parity result fixes alpha to 0.05, statistical power to 0.80, the test direction to directional, and the inverse-square-root constant to 2.486.
A settings surface cannot relabel another alpha, power, or test direction as this documented SmartPLS result.

acceptance_items.description: The documented result has one fixed assumption set rather than an inferred default that may silently change.
acceptance_criteria: A new result records 0.05, 0.80, directional, and 2.486 explicitly in its analytical payload.
Save/reopen and every export reproduce those assumptions exactly.

acceptance_items.description: The result belongs to a completed PLS-SEM algorithm model and is driven by an eligible structural path coefficient; it is not a generic output of every algorithm.
acceptance_criteria: The table is created only for a completed PLS-SEM algorithm result containing at least one eligible structural path.
PCA, CB-SEM, regression, and other algorithm families cannot emit this parity table merely because they contain coefficients.

acceptance_items.description: The diagnostic uses the structural estimates and valid analytical observation count from the same completed PLS run.
acceptance_criteria: The stored analytical sample size equals the valid observation count used for the linked PLS estimation.
Changing the dataset, missing-data treatment, or path estimates invalidates the stored diagnostic instead of reusing it.

acceptance_items.description: The original inverse-square-root rule uses the statistically significant structural path with the smallest absolute magnitude; focal relevance remains an interpretation caution rather than an undocumented numerical rewrite.
acceptance_criteria: An inference-aware parity implementation selects the statistically significant eligible path having the smallest absolute coefficient, with a documented deterministic tie rule.
A point-estimate-only smallest-path fallback is identified as a QuickPLS difference and cannot satisfy full parity coverage.
Control, exploratory, or substantively irrelevant paths are never silently removed from the numerical rule; any focal-path selection must be explicit and separately identified.

acceptance_items.description: The result is labeled Technically required sample size and reports the ceiling of the inverse-square-root calculation for the driver coefficient.
acceptance_criteria: For absolute coefficients 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30, and 0.40 the required sample sizes are respectively 619, 275, 155, 99, 69, and 39.
The result links the required count, analytical count, driver path, fixed assumptions, and adequacy comparison to the same run.
The result states that technical adequacy does not establish population representativeness, causal validity, or general study quality.

acceptance_items.description: The official workflow documents a result value and interpretation table, not a required analytical chart.
acceptance_criteria: Parity does not require a chart for this result.
Any optional QuickPLS visualization is clearly additional and reproduces the same stored coefficient-to-sample-size calculation.

acceptance_items.description: The result must distinguish inapplicability from mathematically large requirements and must not turn representativeness or substantive relevance into unsupported claims.
acceptance_criteria: A model without an eligible structural path returns a typed not-applicable result.
Zero and near-zero driver coefficients never overflow, clamp, or produce NaN; an unrepresentable requirement returns a typed unavailable state.
A very large finite requirement remains visible with the documented near-zero-effect explanation rather than being classified as a calculation error.

acceptance_items.description: The documented workflow opens the result after PLS-SEM estimation under Algorithm -> Posthoc minimum sample size, compares it with the valid analytical sample, and keeps bootstrap inference and prospective planning separate.
acceptance_criteria: A user can open the linked table from a completed PLS run, compare required and analytical sample sizes, and export the same values.
The workflow explains that post-hoc diagnosis does not replace a priori planning or bootstrap inference.
Subgroup, multigroup, missing-data, and complex-sampling cautions remain visible where relevant.
